messages:
eli: Running into a crash on Windows embeddable Python 3.8 when creating AsyncClient — CI fails but local linux ok. Trace below. Anyone seen an env/packaging quirk like this?

eli: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/test_connect.py", line 8, in test_connect
    client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")
  File "/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 34, in __init__
    self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(ssl=self._build_ssl_context())
  File "/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 78, in _build_ssl_context
    ctx.load_verify_locations(cafile=certifi.where())
NameError: name 'certifi' is not defined
```

rachael: That NameError smells like certifi wasn't imported in that module. But why only on embeddable/3.8? Are we shipping certifi as an extra or relying on system install?

tim: Checking wheel metadata now 50d. I see in setup.cfg we put certifi in extras_require["ssl"] instead of install_requires. Oops. Most installs pick it up transitively on linux (envs with requests) but embeddable CI uses a minimal pip install and doesn't pull extras.

eli: Yep that matches: pip freeze in failing CI shows no certifi package. Local dev had certifi installed via other deps so it masked the bug.

tim: Short-term workaround: import certifi guardedly and fall back to ssl.create_default_context() if unavailable. But long-term we should move certifi into install_requires or have the client dynamically use certifi if present but not crash if absent.

sam: Also flag: our typed stubs export `Client` in the top-level __init__ but not `AsyncClient` which makes mypy/IDE users accidentally import sync client and get attribute errors on async methods. We should update py.typed and __all__ so IDEs show both variants.

rachael: Agree. Proposed checklist in issue: 1) Move certifi -> install_requires. 2) Defensive import+fallback in async/sync client so NameError doesn't kill imports. 3) Add unit test simulating missing certifi. 4) Update typing exports and add simple docs note about embeddable Windows.

tim: Draft patch in branch fix/ssl-certifi-ship. Example defensive snippet I pushed to PR comment: 
```python
# in redwood/async_client.py
import ssl
try:
    import certifi
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - CI matrix will catch this path
    certifi = None

def _build_ssl_context():
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    if certifi is not None:
        try:
            ctx.load_verify_locations(cafile=certifi.where())
            logger.debug("Using certifi CA bundle at %s", certifi.where())
        except Exception:
            logger.debug("certifi present but failed to load, falling back to system CA")
    return ctx
```

eli: Nice. For sync code path we should do the same and for any internal HTTP helpers. Add a debug log so users on Windows can see we used certifi.

devx-bot: Filed canonical issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/issues/1302 (certifi in extras + async client NameError + typing export). CI job request: add windows-embeddable-3.8 to the GH actions matrix.

rachael: Also adding a note to onboarding quickstart: "If you're using Windows embeddable Python, ensure certifi is installed or upgrade SDK v0.13+ which auto-handles CA bundles."

tim: Will open the PR to move certifi to install_requires and add the defensive import. Tests: adding a tox env that uninstalls certifi and asserts client creation doesn't NameError and still raises a clear SSL error if no CA (so we don't silently accept insecure).

eli: One more DX thing: the typed stubs for AsyncClient are missing `__aenter__/__aexit__` signatures which makes `async with AsyncClient(...) as c:` flag in IDEs. Add those to stubs.

sam: Great callout. I'll add that to the PR checklist. Also request we add a short paragraph to docs explaining the difference between embeddable vs system python and certs on Windows.

rachael: ETA: PR and CI update by EOD tomorrow. Leaving the QA label for folks who run Windows embeddable locally to confirm.

eli: Thanks all 44d. Saved our CI pipeline.

devx-bot: Linking docs stub: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python#windows-embeddable-cert-quirks (todo entry created).
